summary: The note surveys the shift in special education from segregation to inclusion, covering history, global approaches, classroom practice, technology, teacher training, funding and measurement. It highlights examples such as IDEA in the US, Kenya's policy framework, Finland's teacher training and New Zealand's toolkit. It stresses that policies vary by region and that full inclusion is an incremental, collaborative journey.
one_line: Overview of how special education has moved toward inclusion, with global examples, challenges around culture, technology, training, funding and measuring success.
key_facts: The Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) was first enacted in the US on October 14, 1975, and has been reauthorized several times, the most recent being after September 1, 2023.
IDEA guarantees students with disabilities the right to a free appropriate public education in the least restrictive environment possible.
Special education programs began to take shape in the early 20th century, when people with disabilities were often educated in separate schools or institutions.
Kenya's Education Cabinet Secretary George Omore launched the National Special Needs Education Policy Framework on November 19, 2023.
Dr. Susan Hartley said inclusivity is about 'actively tailoring the teaching and learning process to ensure that everyone participates fully,' not just physical placement.
Riverdale Elementary, under Principal John Frederick, reported marked improvements in student engagement after adopting differentiated instruction in spring 2024.
Scandinavian countries are praised for inclusive education, supported by high taxation and extensive social services, which makes their policies hard to export.
Professor Anne Clarkson of the University of Melbourne found technology significantly increased autonomy and engagement of special needs students after its implementation in 2025.
The International Association for Special Education reported that many teachers still feel inadequately prepared for diverse student needs.
Finland prioritizes special education teacher training, with programs run by educators like Markus Heikkinen, and has had a smoother transition to inclusive practices.
Emily Johnson of the National Center for Learning Disabilities campaigns for the full federal funding of IDEA promised since the act's inception.
The New Zealand Ministry of Education initiated the Inclusive Practices Toolkit in January 2026 to help evaluate inclusive practices, including social-emotional learning benchmarks.
